handDesc.handNote: Main text and any darker interventions are distinguished where observed. No individual historical correcting hands are inferred from tonal contrast in monochrome photographs.

origin.p: The supplied BnF IIIF manifest dates the manuscript to 1001–1100. The catalogue dating is not a date assigned to individual interventions.

surrogates.p: The original full-resolution digital images and enlarged crops were inspected for this first pass. Gallica source reuse conditions apply. No text was populated from LL or another witness.

projectDesc.p: Source-grounded first reading of all 84 annotated verse positions, with manuscript-specific spellings and observed interventions. A different agent subsequently inspected all source verses and every evidence note; see revision record and second-pass ledger.

correction.p: No silent emendation from an edition or another witness. Local uncertain letters use unclear, irrecoverable text or signs use gap. Observed above-line letters use add. Tonal distinctions use hi without an invented underlying erased text or historical hand. Manuscript annotations use note type manuscript, distinct from editorial evidence notes.

normalization.p: One source-oriented display. Ordinary allographs, long s, and capitals are represented in legible Latin types. Word boundaries are editorially segmented; no indentation whitespace is inserted inside verse mixed content. Selected ligatures and abbreviation signs are declared typographic approximations; explicit expansions remain in TEI rather than a separate reading mode. This is not a facsimile-perfect inventory of every minute stroke.

punctuation.p: Significant observed punctuation is retained schematically, without adding systematic modern sentence punctuation.

segmentation.p: Each l represents a verse and physical written line at its canonical poem position. Elegiac couplets and even-line indentation are editorial display grouping. Page breaks follow the photographed left/right physical pages. Facsimile zones reproduce the existing annotation rectangles unchanged; they may include neighbouring ink and exclude marginal annotations.

interpretation.p: First-pass evidence notes are a working queue for an independent agent, not assignments for the human editor. Genuine source uncertainty remains local; consequential unresolved interpretation is distinguished from ordinary observation.

revisionDesc.change: Independent second-agent source review of all 84 verses and every editorial note. Corrected circo to circum at65 and revised the uncertain final vowel of rato at81; all prior uncertainties and the actual addition om at62 remain explicit. No human approval is implied.
Completed first reading from source images and enlarged crops, with line coverage and evidence notes. Independent second reading not yet performed.

div.head: Independently reviewed source notes
div.note: A small two-line marginal heading accompanies the large initial N. The faded tentative reading ad amicam / in circus is encoded as a manuscript note, with local uncertainty. The line zone does not encompass all of this heading. No hand identity is asserted.
The ending of esset uses a ligature-like et form; the visible form is represented schematically with an explicit expansion, without introducing a second display text.

A diagonal physical obstruction crosses the upper right page around lines 5–7. The visible sequence is retained; the material cause and historical date of the obstruction are not inferred. Wider page margins also contain faint traces whose status and text are not securely recoverable.
The visible word after manibus reads rora in this image: its first letter lacks the tall ascender of lora in line 11. The source reading is retained without a silent correction.
The visible final word is represented asta; no h has been silently restored. Spelling pisaea likewise follows the photograph.
The vowel before final s in spectas is faint and locally uncertain; the source-oriented reading is not normalized to an expected form.
The personal-name sequence milanion atlantis is severely faded. A tentative continuous reading is retained in unclear rather than asserted as certain.
The diagonal obstruction crosses arsi at the opening of the left page. Its partly visible reading is marked unclear; no wholly lost letters have been supplied as established text.
The diagonal obstruction also crosses the short word read ex. Local uncertainty preserves the partial source evidence.
The final word is visibly manu. No final s is supplied from grammatical expectation.
The short word following castora is faded; placet remains a tentative reading after independent inspection of the local strokes.
A dark patch overlaps the central phrase in lines 57–58. The readings dominae patiatur and secunda are retained locally as unclear. The patch is not encoded as a scribal deletion.
The middle of promittas is faint and physically disturbed; the tentative word remains unclear. No invented underlying cancellation is asserted.
The letters om stand above the baseline between in and ne. They are encoded as an above-line addition completing omne, without assigning a correcting hand or conjecturing a deletion.
The sequence in the photograph is Sint mea sint dominae fac rata uota meae, followed by Sunt dominae rato uota meae mea uota supersunt. Both distinct opening verbs and the repetitions are retained.
The end of the enlarged line reads circum, including faint final nasal strokes, rather than first-pass circo.
The final vowel of the word after dominae is rounded, favoring rato. It is less securely differentiated in this faded stretch, so the revised o remains local unclear.
